plain_explanation: For tax payments relating to periods before Tax Year 2026-27, use the Income-tax Act, 1961.
applicability_note: This is a historical boundary through 31 March 2026. Confirm the relevant payment or assessment period before identifying a section.

plain_explanation: For tax-year questions from 1 April 2026, use the Income-tax Act, 2025 as amended by Finance Act, 2026. Earlier assessment or payment periods can remain governed by the Income-tax Act, 1961.
applicability_note: Ask for the transaction, payment or relevant tax-year date before naming a section when the period is unclear.

topic: Section 196 short-term gains on specified equity assets
plain_explanation: Section 196 states a 20% short-term capital-gains rate for covered equity shares, equity-oriented funds and business trusts where its securities-transaction-tax conditions are met.
applicability_note: Applies only to the specified asset and STT-paid transaction conditions in Section 196. It is not a personal tax calculation.
official_source_title: Income-tax Act, 2025 as amended by Finance Act, 2026

topic: Section 198 long-term gains on specified equity assets
plain_explanation: Section 198 applies a 12.5% rate to aggregate covered long-term gains above ₹1,25,000 when its listed-equity, equity-oriented-fund or business-trust and STT conditions are satisfied.
applicability_note: An ETF must first meet the equity-oriented-fund definition. The ₹1,25,000 threshold and STT conditions are statutory boundaries, not a calculation for an individual.
official_source_title: Income-tax Act, 2025 as amended by Finance Act, 2026

plain_explanation: The equity-oriented-fund definition has statutory investment conditions. TaxEd must not treat every exchange-traded fund as an equity-oriented fund without checking that definition.
applicability_note: Use this boundary before applying Sections 196 or 198 to an ETF or mutual-fund unit.
official_source_title: Income-tax Act, 2025 as amended by Finance Act, 2026

plain_explanation: Section 197 sets a 12.5% general long-term capital-gains rule without indexation, subject to the Act's asset-specific sections and exceptions.
applicability_note: Do not use this general rule where a specific statutory rule, holding-period condition or exception applies.
official_source_title: Income-tax Act, 2025 as amended by Finance Act, 2026

topic: Section 76 short-term boundary for specified debt assets
plain_explanation: Section 76 treats specified debt mutual funds, market-linked debentures and unlisted bonds as short-term capital assets in the stated cases.
applicability_note: Check the instrument type and the precise statutory conditions. A listed bond is not automatically within the stated unlisted-bond boundary.
official_source_title: Income-tax Act, 2025 as amended by Finance Act, 2026

plain_explanation: From 1 April 2026, Section 69 treats buy-back consideration less acquisition cost as capital gains.
applicability_note: Promoter-related additions and facts outside the stated rule need qualified Indian tax-professional review.
official_source_title: Income-tax Act, 2025 as amended by Finance Act, 2026

plain_explanation: From 1 April 2026, Section 93(2) provides that no deduction shall be allowed for any dividend income, income from units of a Mutual Fund specified under Schedule VII (Table: Sl. No. 20 or 21) or income from units of a specified company referred to in section 2(h) of the Unit Trust of India (Transfer of Undertaking and Repeal) Act, 2002.
applicability_note: Applies to the dividend and covered mutual-fund-unit income described in Section 93(2). The applicable rate depends on facts outside this registry.
official_source_title: Income-tax Act, 2025 as amended by Finance Act, 2026

topic: GST on physical gold and covered jewellery
plain_explanation: Physical gold and covered jewellery attract 3% GST on the relevant transaction value under the GST rate schedule.
applicability_note: This rule is for physical gold and covered jewellery. It does not establish GST treatment for gold ETFs or sovereign gold bonds.
official_source_title: CBIC Notification No. 1/2017-Central Tax (Rate), Schedule V

topic: Securities Transaction Tax on specified derivatives from 2026
plain_explanation: From 1 April 2026, the stated STT rates are 0.15% on option sale, 0.15% for the purchaser of an exercised option and 0.05% on futures sale by the seller.
applicability_note: Applies to the specified exchange-traded derivatives transaction and party. It is an exchange-collected transaction tax, not a capital-gains rate.

plain_explanation: A listed bond can fall under the Act's listed-security long-term treatment when its applicable holding-period condition is met. The Section 76 unlisted-bond rule is a separate short-term boundary.
applicability_note: Confirm listing status, instrument type and holding period before applying a long-term rule. Unlisted bonds require the separate Section 76 check.
official_source_title: Income-tax Act, 2025 as amended by Finance Act, 2026
